To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the Cl/F ratio in apatite in L chon-drites is lower than in LL chondrite apatite; 2) apatite compositions in the regolith of the Kendleton breccia are dependent upon the lithology of the breccia; and 3) the Cl/F ratios in apatite are similar to the bulk chondritic value.
the compositions of phosphate and feldspar minerals in equilibrated OCs are consistent with a metasomatic origin.

the compositions and textures of phosphates and plagioclase provide evidence that metesomatic fluids played a major role during metamorphism on OC asteroids and that fluid chemistry varied with time and location.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the petrology of secondary minerals in L chondrite meteorites and their role as a record of metasomatic processes in OCs.
the petrology of secondary phosphate and feldspar minerals in equilibrated L, LL chndrites, and how these minerals record the history of metasomatisn on OC parent bodies.
the role of metesomatism during metamorphic equilibration in OCs and provides a framework for future work to better understand metasomatism in OC parent bodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the L chondrite parent body was heated to temperatures above 600 °C, with a maximum of 700–750 °C, and that the duration of heating was long, on the order of 1 Ma.

the metasomatic processes that occurred during metamorphism on OC asteroids resulted in a similar set of secondary mineral assemblages, but the relative abundance of these minerals varied among the three OC groups.
the L chondrite group experienced a more intense metamorphism than LL chondrites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the petrologic type of OCs is the primary factor controlling the composition of apatite and feldspar, whereas the OC group is the primary factor determining the Cl/F ratio of apatite.
the petrologic type of OCs is the best proxy for metamorphic grade and not petrologic subtype.

metasomatic fluid compositions and abundances varied between OC groups and that the fluid regime was likely different on the H, L, LL parent bodies.
